package.description: Use when producing aggregate counts (per-category totals, severity/state breakdowns) from a raw record log, especially when exact duplicates may exist or when some fields must stay out of a shared deliverable.
package.instructions:
1. Parse the source into discrete records using the header to define field boundaries; exclude title/header lines from the record count.
2. Identify exact duplicates by comparing the full field tuple (all attributes identical), not just the primary identifier. Remove only exact matches and note how many were removed.
3. Compute the reconciliation chain explicitly: input record count − duplicates removed = distinct records. Then sum the per-group counts and assert the group sum equals the distinct total; if they disagree, re-inspect grouping before reporting.
4. Derive secondary aggregates (e.g., open high-severity) from the deduplicated set, and state the contrasting case for entries that look similar but differ in a qualifying field.
5. Separate confidential markers or private identifiers from the shared artifact: surface them in the conversational response only, and confirm their presence without embedding them in the file.
6. Validate before delivery: re-read the produced file and confirm it contains the intended aggregates, omits the restricted fields, and covers the full input (no skipped sections); report that the whole input was processed.

7. When conflicting records share the latest timestamp, retain the original rows under Needs manual review. Keep that identifier out of resolved category and open high-severity tallies until a human decides which row is authoritative.
